title: SMB Vector Search: Model Submarket Heatmap & Buyer's Journey Recon
creator: Asha Patel
description: Synthesize a concise, decision-oriented deliverable mapping the model submarket for vector search (SMB horizontal use cases) and overlay buyer-journey signals to identify 3 high-value model+config archetypes Redwood should explicitly support and benchmark. Deliverable is a 1-page heatmap + 2-page notes pack for GTM/engineers.
background: SMB customers frequently cite embeddings/vector search as a top use case but are price-sensitive and operationally limited. Existing model watch artifacts focus on enterprise substitutes and broad LLM features; we lack a lightweight submarket map targeted at small-to-medium SaaS buyers (embedding latency/throughput, quantization friendliness, licensing, footprint). This ticket scopes research and product recommendations that can be consumed by solutions engineering and pricing.
goals: Produce a model submarket heatmap with axes: unit cost (tokens/embedding) vs operational friction (memory + quantization support).
Surface 3 SKU-level model archetypes (low-cost hybrid quantized, balanced, high-accuracy moderate-cost) with recommended default config knobs for Redwood Optimize rules.
Map buyer journey triggers and gate criteria (trial, POC, scale thresholds) to rollback/rollout policies for Dedicated vs Hosted routing.
Create an exec 1-pager and a detailed 2-page appendix with dataset/benchmarks and signal sources.
scope: Include open models and popular commercial variants that SMBs commonly evaluate (open 2.x/3.x, small Llama forks, hosted embeddings providers). Exclude multimodal/voice workloads and pure enterprise-only custom model integrations. Run lightweight microbenchmarks on token-limited sample queries and 50k embedding batch sim. Use existing Redwood benchmarking harness where possible.
success_metrics: 1-page heatmap validated by 2 field interviews with solutions engineers
Adoption: at least 1 feature/experiment in Redwood Optimize referencing the recommended archetypes within 6 weeks
Clarity: GTM/sales can reference the 1-page pack in qualifying calls (measured by 3 sales feedbacks)
research_summary: Initial reconnaissance (Nov–Dec 2025) surveyed 12 public benchmarks and 6 vendor docs. Early signal shows a bifurcation: (a) tiny quantized models excel on latency/cost but have variable semantic recall on long-tail SMB datasets; (b) mid-sized open models provide a better accuracy/cost sweet spot for semantic search at 512-dim vectors. We ran a 4-model microbenchmark (OpenTiny-quant, OpenMid-8bit, LlamaS-7B-ptq, CommercialEmbedX) using the Redwood harness: latency variance under 128 batch is the dominant UX issue for trial users. Detailed results linked below.
